findings.title: The `repo` argument lets the row execute git in a repository OUTSIDE the workspace, from the unsandboxed plugin process
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts :: resolveRepo / createWorktree / mergeWorktree / removeWorktree; packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/git.ts :: runGit
findings.evidence: reviewer probe P25: with DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT=<ws>, `mpd_worktree_create {name:'x', repo:'<other repo>'}` created branch agent/x in <other repo> while the worktree path stayed inside <ws>; git runs via spawnSync in the harness process, so no `workspace-write` fence applies
findings.whyItMatters: D2 protects the worktree PATH only: the plugin's own git calls are not sandboxed, so a member (or any session holding these tools) can create/delete branches and worktrees in unrelated local repositories. The contract makes `repo` an argument, so this is not a contract violation — but docs/worktree.md's Declared bounds do not mention it, and a reasonable user would expect a member's worktree operations to stay inside the workspace.
findings.direction: Either confine `repo`/`worktree.repo` to a path under the workspace root (or a configured allowlist) with a typed refusal, or add the bound to docs/worktree.md §Declared bounds + README, and state it in the PR body.

findings.title: `cwdForMember` hands a reseed a recorded path WITHOUT the 'git still manages it' guard that `recordOf` applies — and inside such a directory git resolves to the MAIN checkout
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts :: cwdForMember (exists-only check) vs the same file's recordOf (`managed = registered.has(canonicalPath(entry.path))` with the explicit stale-directory comment)
findings.evidence: reviewer probe P26: create a member worktree, delete its `.git` link out of band, then cwdForMember still returns the path and `git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers the MAIN workspace root on branch `main`
findings.whyItMatters: The reseed would hand that directory as the child's EFFECTIVE cwd, and the member's git commands would then operate on the main checkout's HEAD — the exact D5 violation this wave exists to prevent. Reachability is bounded: it needs out-of-band damage (a pruned registration or a removed `.git` link), not a normal API sequence; that is why it ranks Medium rather than High.
findings.direction: Apply recordOf's membership check inside cwdForMember (answer undefined when git no longer lists the path, so the reseed degrades to the shared checkout), or verify the worktree's `.git` link resolves under `<repo>/.git/worktrees/`.

findings.title: An index write that fails AFTER `git worktree add` leaves an orphan worktree no tool can remove
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts :: createEntry (addWorktree then writeIndex inside withLock)
findings.evidence: code read: the branch+directory are created before the record; on a writeIndex throw the tree exists unrecorded, and a retry refuses with `path-exists` while `mpd_worktree_remove` refuses with `unknown-worktree`
findings.whyItMatters: A recovery then needs manual `git worktree remove`/`branch -D` — a small operational trap, never silent data loss (worktree add is a no-op if the path already exists).
findings.direction: Prune the just-created worktree/branch when the index write throws, or document the manual recovery line in the README bounds.
